bull.b: Completing enrollment in the IgA nephropathy cohort provides a defined clinical development milestone, while adding a focal segmental glomerulosclerosis cohort broadens testing across complement-mediated kidney diseases. This expands the potential application of vensobafusp alfa and supports pipeline progress over the next several quarters.

A $132 million PIPE that extends operating runway into the second half of 2028 gives Jasper additional time to advance clinical programs before needing new financing. Greater funding visibility can support trial execution, regulatory work and strategic development while reducing near-term dependence on capital markets.

Retiring outstanding warrants can simplify the capital structure and reduce the number of shares that might otherwise be issued through future exercises. Although the action uses cash, limiting this potential dilution may provide existing shareholders with clearer ownership economics as the pipeline advances.

bear.b: Jasper remains pre-commercial, with no product revenue to fund research, clinical development or corporate expenses. Continued losses mean the business has not yet demonstrated operating leverage, and future financial performance remains dependent on clinical progress, regulatory approval and eventual commercialization or partnering.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow shows that Jasper’s current activities consume capital rather than generate it. Even with improvement from 2025 levels, ongoing burn can require additional financing over time, potentially constraining development choices or increasing shareholder dilution.

bear.t: Weakening balance sheet and dilution risk
bear.b: The sharp decline in equity materially reduces the balance-sheet cushion available to absorb continued losses. The approved increase in authorized shares also gives the company greater financing capacity, but it can raise future dilution risk as Jasper funds development without recurring product revenue.
